name: seb-benchmark-platform-throughput
description: Measurement-throughput and output-budget constraints of the /workspace benchmark gateway that dominate suite design
metadata:
  type: project
---

On the /workspace executable-benchmark platform (research_sdk `Client`), candidate calls
**must** go through `Client.submit(path, model=...)`; a direct `Client.chat()` to a
development model from the researcher context returns HTTP 403. Only 2 suites run
concurrently and only 2 requests per model, running jobs cannot be cancelled (409, queued
ones can), and partial `result.json` is not retrievable until a job reaches `ok`. A
108-item suite took ~75 minutes wall clock for one model, so a 4-model development round
needs ~2.5 hours in two waves — budget the research clock around that, not around dollars.

Output budget is the dominant measurement artifact: at 12000 max_tokens, `development-01`
(effort `xhigh`) truncated 36/102 items with `finish_reason == "max_tokens"`, 32 of them
returning empty text, concentrated on research-math and code-implementation items. Set
per-item budgets to ~24k for hard reasoning and ~16k for code implementation, and always
inspect `finish_reason` before believing a low score.

Related: [[seb-benchmark-visible-target-ceilings]]
"
}

name: seb-benchmark-visible-target-ceilings
description: The visible coding references in whitebox.json conflict, capping the attainable macro Pearson near 0.77
metadata:
  type: project
---

For the /workspace joint coding / co-work / reasoning benchmark, the eight visible
reference targets in `whitebox.json` are mutually inconsistent inside the coding domain:
DeepSWE ranks the development models 01 > 08 > 12 > 06 while SWE-bench Multilingual ranks
08 > 12 > 06 > 01, and SWE Atlas spans only 44.9-46.0 across three models (its own noise
floor). A grid search over all measured-score shapes puts the best attainable average
Pearson for coding at about **+0.31 for any single measured score**; co-work and reasoning
both admit ~+1.0. So the macro objective (three domains averaged equally) is bounded near
**0.77**, and effort is best spent on co-work and reasoning.

Target-implied ideal shapes: coding 01 > 12 > 08 >> 06; co-work 12 >> 01 > 06 ~ 08;
reasoning 01 >> 12 > 08 > 06. Useful for sanity-checking a measured profile, never for
fitting scores.

Related: [[seb-benchmark-platform-throughput]]
"
}

108	## Frozen domain aggregation
109	
110	`evaluation.json:domain_aggregations` declares one `weighted_mean` per domain over the

112	
113	```
114	domain_score = sum_i w_i * grade_i / sum_i w_i     over completed items i of the domain
115	```
116	
117	Items that did not complete are excluded from both numerator and denominator, and the
118	missing coverage is reported in the result rows. The same three measured scores are used
119	unchanged for every reference benchmark in the corresponding domain.
120	
121	Weights are **uniform**: every question in a domain carries weight 1.0, so the domain score
122	is the plain mean of that domain's item grades. No per-item weight is tuned, no weight was
123	fitted to any reference label, and no family is up- or down-weighted after seeing results.
124	Uniform weighting was chosen over family- or source-balanced alternatives because the
125	families differ in size by an order of magnitude (2 to 26 items), and balancing would give
126	the two-item test-authoring family the same influence as the twelve execution-graded coding
127	tasks, which is a variance trade this suite cannot afford with only a handful of models.

129	Item counts per domain: `coding` 22, `co-work` 28, `reasoning` 58.

137	
138	Per-item output budgets are part of the frozen protocol and were set from a completed
